title: fix: keep `snippets.json` out of VM configuration scans
body:
## Problem

When `VEX_CONFIG_DIR` is set, `snippets_file()` stores the user snippet library at `$VEX_CONFIG_DIR/snippets.json`. Both the CLI list command and the TUI scanner inspect every `*.json` file in that directory as if it were a `QemuConfig`.

The CLI silently skips the snippet file after deserialization fails, while the TUI exposes it as a broken configuration named `snippets`. After a user saves a snippet in Library mode, the Browse view can therefore show a false broken VM entry.

## Suggested scope

- Treat `snippets.json` as reserved metadata when enumerating VM configuration files.
- Apply the same file-selection rule to the CLI list path, the TUI scanner, and other config-directory scans where appropriate.
- Do not hide genuinely malformed VM configuration files from the TUI.
- A small shared predicate is welcome if it avoids duplicating filename rules.

## Acceptance criteria

- With `VEX_CONFIG_DIR` set and a valid snippet library at `$VEX_CONFIG_DIR/snippets.json`, the TUI scan does not return a `ConfigEntry` named `snippets`.
- Normal `<name>.json` VM configs are still listed.
- A malformed VM config such as `broken-vm.json` is still surfaced as `ConfigEntry::Broken`.
- Add regression tests for the explicit-`VEX_CONFIG_DIR` layout.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --all-targets` pass.

## Relevant files

- `src/snippets/storage.rs`
- `src/commands/list.rs`
- `src/tui/scan.rs`
- `src/commands/cache.rs`
- `src/tests/test_list.rs`
- `src/tests/test_tui.rs`

title: fix: include all current subcommands in generated Zsh completions
body:
## Problem

`print_zsh_dynamic_completion()` replaces the Clap-generated `_vex` function with a hard-coded subcommand list. That list currently omits `resource`, `cache`, `hub`, and `tui`, even though the same function already contains argument-handling branches for `resource` and `cache`.

As a result, generated Zsh completions do not advertise all commands supported by `vex --help`.

## Suggested scope

- Update the Zsh completion overlay so every variant of `commands::Commands` is discoverable.
- Prefer an approach that reduces the chance of the hard-coded list drifting again; a focused synchronization test is sufficient if reusing the generated command metadata would make the change too large.
- Preserve dynamic configuration-name and cache-hash completion behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- `vex completions zsh` includes `save`, `rename`, `rm`, `list`, `print`, `pull`, `push`, `exec`, `completions`, `edit`, `resource`, `cache`, `hub`, and `tui`.
- Existing dynamic completion helpers remain in the generated script.
- `src/tests/test_completions.rs` asserts the complete Zsh command set so future additions cannot silently drift.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --all-targets` pass.

## Relevant files

- `src/commands/completions.rs`
- `src/commands/mod.rs`
- `src/tests/test_completions.rs`

title: feat: show bound resources in `vex print` output
body:
## Problem

`vex print <NAME>` describes the binary and arguments of a saved configuration, but it omits the configuration's `resources` map. Users must run a separate `vex resource list <NAME>` command to see which files are bound to `${res:KEY}` placeholders.

The TUI details pane and `resource list` already contain examples of how resource data can be displayed.

## Suggested scope

- Add a **Resources** section to `vex print`.
- Sort resource keys before printing so the output is deterministic.
- For each resource, show the key, kind, path, and optional SHA-256, size, and URL using clear placeholders when metadata is absent.
- Preserve all existing sections and their current wording.

## Acceptance criteria

- A configuration with multiple resources prints every resource in key-sorted order.
- Resource kind and path are always shown; optional metadata is represented clearly when present or absent.
- A configuration without resources has an unambiguous empty state or omits the section consistently with the chosen design.
- Add integration coverage in `src/tests/test_print.rs`.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --all-targets` pass.

## Relevant files

- `src/commands/print.rs`
- `src/commands/resource.rs` (output reference)
- `src/tui/render/right_pane.rs` (output reference)
- `src/tests/test_print.rs`

title: fix: sort `vex list` output by configuration name
body:
## Problem

`vex list` currently prints configurations in the order returned by `std::fs::read_dir`. That order is filesystem-dependent, so the same configuration directory can produce different output across systems or runs.

The TUI scanner already sorts entries by name in `src/tui/scan.rs`; the CLI should behave consistently.

## Suggested scope

- Sort the collected configurations by name before printing them in `src/commands/list.rs`.
- Use the same ascending, case-sensitive ordering as `scan_configs()`.
- Keep the existing output format unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- `vex list` prints configuration names in ascending order even when files were created in a different order.
- Existing description, QEMU binary, and argument output is unchanged.
- Add a regression test in `src/tests/test_list.rs` that creates configs in non-alphabetical order and asserts their positions in stdout.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --all-targets` pass.

## Relevant files

- `src/commands/list.rs`
- `src/tests/test_list.rs`

title: Vex 0.4.1 — Edit mode, Snippets, and Library
body:
Second milestone of Phase 4. The TUI evolves from a launcher into
a full configuration editor, with a curated library of 42 QEMU
argument snippets to make common setups trivial.

## Changes

### Added
- **Snippet library system**: 42 curated builtin QEMU argument
  snippets across 8 categories (Memory, CPU, Machine, Storage,
  Network, Display, Debug, Kernel) plus a `~/.vex/snippets.json`
  user library for custom entries. User snippets merge with builtins,
  with user entries overriding by name.
- **TUI Edit mode**: press `e` on a configuration to edit it
  in-place, or `n` to create a new one. Fields: name, QEMU binary,
  description, and args (with reorder, delete, add, and in-place
  token editing). Resources remain CLI-managed.
- **TUI Snippets drawer** (Edit mode right pane): merged snippets
  grouped by category with fold/unfold, filter, and `→` to insert
  into the current args position.
- **TUI Library mode** (`Ctrl+L`): full-screen snippet manager.
  Browse with details panel; `n` / `e` / `d` to create, edit, or
  delete user snippets. Persists to `~/.vex/snippets.json` via
  atomic write (temp-file + rename). Builtin snippets are read-only.
- **Args token editing**: in Edit mode and Library snippet edit,
  press `Enter` on an arg to edit its string in place, or `a` to add
  an empty arg and immediately start editing it.

### Changed
- **Edit mode `Tab` semantics**: `Tab` switches between the Editor
  and Snippets panes; field cycling within the Editor uses `↑` / `↓`.

### Notes
- Snippets file uses `schema_version: 1`. Forward-compatible
  deserialization is planned for a later release.
- Carry-over from 0.4.0 development: help overlay is panic-safe on
  tiny terminals, right-pane scroll clamps and writes back,
  `Ctrl+C` always quits regardless of mode/overlay.

## Verification

- `cargo build` / `cargo test` (495 passed, 1 ignored) /
  `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` / `cargo fmt --check` /
  `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps` — all clean
- Implementation split across two commits:
  - `feat(snippets): data layer with 42 builtin entries and user library merge`
  - `feat(tui): Edit mode, Snippets drawer, and Library mode (0.4.1)`

## Pending (not blocking)

- Screenshots for the new Edit mode and Library mode will be added
  to README after a manual TTY pass. README has placeholders.
- 0.4.2 backlog: Schema v3 with category field, tree grouping view,
  Hub async fetching.

title: adds the vex tui — an interactive terminal UI for browsing and launching saved QEMU configurations.
body:
# Vex 0.4.0 Review Brief

This PR adds the `vex tui` subcommand (Phase 4 milestone 1) — an interactive 
terminal UI for browsing and launching saved QEMU configurations.

## Scope of review

5 indivisible commits implementing the full TUI from scratch:

- **P4-1** Extract `prepare_command` from `exec_command` (CLI/TUI shared 
  preparation logic)
- **P4-2** ratatui 0.28 + crossterm 0.28 dependencies, empty TUI shell, panic 
  hook, `vex tui` subcommand with hidden `--exit-after-init` test flag
- **P4-3** Browse mode: two-pane layout (list + details), keyboard navigation 
  (j/k/g/G/Tab), right-pane scrolling, broken-config tolerance
- **P4-4** Enter to launch QEMU: 5-step terminal hand-off (leave alt-screen → 
  disable raw → run QEMU → re-enable raw → re-enter alt-screen → clear), 
  resource pre-flight check, error reporting via status bar
- **P4-5** Filter sub-mode, Help overlay, Refresh, headless test harness, 
  release bookkeeping

Total: +2365 LOC, tests 308 → 375 (+67), 1 ignored (L3 TTY-required).

## Areas of highest concern (please weight your review accordingly)

### 1. Terminal hand-off correctness (P4-4)
File: `src/tui/runner.rs`, function `launch_selected_config`.

The function executes a precise 5-step sequence for safely letting QEMU own 
the terminal and reclaiming it afterwards. Any reorder or skipped step risks 
leaving the user's terminal in a corrupted state. Please verify:
- Order of `LeaveAlternateScreen` / `disable_raw_mode` / `Show cursor`
- Order of the reverse path: `enable_raw_mode` / `EnterAlternateScreen` / 
  `Hide cursor` / `terminal.clear()`
- Step 4 (re-entry) failures propagate as `VexError` (not best-effort)
- Step 1 (pre-flight `prepare_command`) failures return `Ok(Some(message))` 
  WITHOUT triggering Step 2 (no terminal switch)
- No `unwrap` / `expect` / `panic!` inside this function

### 2. Panic hook (P4-2)
File: `src/tui/runner.rs`, function `install_panic_hook`.

Installs a hook that restores the terminal on panic before delegating to the 
original hook. Please verify it cannot itself panic and that it correctly 
chains to the original.

### 3. translate_key priority order (P4-5)
File: `src/tui/event.rs`, function `translate_key`.

A 5-tier priority table — help-overlay > Press-guard > Ctrl+C > filter-active > 
idle/accepted. Please look for any input mode where a key could be 
mis-interpreted (e.g., Ctrl+C swallowed by filter mode, or `q` triggering Quit 
during filter typing).

### 4. Browse sub-mode state machine (P4-5)
File: `src/tui/app.rs`, `BrowseSubMode` and related handlers.

Filter has three meaningful states: `Idle`, `Filtering { accepted: false }`, 
`Filtering { accepted: true }`. Please verify transitions are consistent — 
especially `selected` and `right_scroll` reset behavior when entering/exiting 
filter mode.

### 5. Resource validation pre-flight (P4-4)
The TUI MUST NOT leave alt-screen if a launch would fail due to missing 
resources or unknown `${res:}` references. Please verify by reading 
`launch_selected_config` Step 1.

## Known carry-overs (NOT bugs)

- **L3 e2e test `tui_command_exits_cleanly_after_init` is `#[ignore]`**: it 
  requires a real TTY which CI typically doesn't provide. Headless test 
  coverage (`run_state_machine`) compensates at the state-machine level. 
  Plan to revisit in 0.4.x with a fuller backend abstraction.
- **Status bar "(press any key to dismiss)" hint uses same color as the 
  message** rather than DIM as originally specified. Cosmetic, considered 
  acceptable for 0.4.0.
- **Resize events are not handled** (the loop redraws every 250 ms anyway, so 
  resize takes effect within one tick). Native resize handling planned for 
  0.4.1+.
- **Screenshots in README** are placeholder text (to be added before GitHub 
  Release).

## What I'm specifically NOT looking for review on

- Edit mode / Library mode / Hub TUI integration (not implemented in 0.4.0)
- Category-based grouping (deferred to 0.4.2 with schema v3)
- L3 TTY-required tests (carried over)

## Test strategy summary

- L1 pure state machine: ~50 tests covering App / Event / scan
- L2 render snapshots via `TestBackend`: ~15 tests asserting visible content 
  on rendered buffers
- L3 headless state-machine driver: 3 tests covering multi-event flows
- L3 TTY-required e2e: 1 test, ignored

title: feat: Add the expression evaluation functionality to the QEMU startup parameters saved in the context
body:
Add the expression evaluation functionality to the QEMU startup parameters saved in the context.

like this:

```
# save context
vex save -d "openeuler-2509" openeuler /home/zevorn/qemu/build/qemu-system-riscv64 \
  -nographic -machine rvsp-ref,pflash0=pflash0,pflash1=pflash1 \
  -smp "$0" -m "$1" \
  -blockdev node-name=pflash0,driver=file,read-only=on,filename="$2" \
  -blockdev node-name=pflash1,driver=file,filename="$3" \
  -object rng-random,filename=/dev/urandom,id=rng0 \
  -drive file="$4",if=virtio,format=qcow2 \
  -fsdev local,security_model=passthrough,id=fsdev0,path=/home/zevorn/openeuler-2509/mnt \
  -device virtio-9p-pci,id=fs0,fsdev=fsdev0,mount_tag=hostshare"

# execute context
# comment         $0 $1    $2                 $3                     $4
vex exec openeuler 8  8G RISCV_VIRT_CODE.fd RISCV_VIRT_VARS.fd openEuler-25.09-riscv64.qcow2


```

title: feat: Add the -f option to the exec command.
body:
Add the -f option to the exec command. The QEMU startup parameters will only be printed when the -f option is added; they will be hidden in all other cases.

like this:

```
vex exec -f openeuler
Starting configuration 'openeuler' (openeuler rvsp-ref): /home/zevorn/oerv/qemu/build/qemu-system-riscv64 ["-nographic", "-machine", "rvsp-ref,pflash0=pflash0,pflash1=pflash1", "-smp", "2", "-m", "8G", "-blockdev", "node-name=pflash0,driver=file,read-only=on,filename=/home/zevorn/openeuler-2509/RISCV_VIRT_CODE.fd", "-blockdev", "node-name=pflash1,driver=file,filename=/home/zevorn/openeuler-2509/RISCV_VIRT_VARS.fd", "-object", "rng-random,filename=/dev/urandom,id=rng0", "-drive", "file=/home/zevorn/openeuler-2509/openEuler-25.09-riscv64.qcow2,if=virtio,format=qcow2", "-fsdev", "local,security_model=passthrough,id=fsdev0,path=/home/zevorn/openeuler-2509/mnt", "-device", "virtio-9p-pci,id=fs0,fsdev=fsdev0,mount_tag=hostshare"]
```

if not `-f`:

```
vex exec openeuler
Starting configuration 'openeuler' (openeuler rvsp-ref)
...
```

Additionally, we can optimize the prompt messages printed by the exec command to make them more user-friendly and visually appealing.
